overview: Both are the process of gamete formation through meiosis, but they differ hugely in timing, output number, and cell size.
genZNote: Spermatogenesis: mass-produces sperm continuously. Oogenesis: carefully produces one egg at a time, keeping most of the cytoplasm for it.

aspects.label: Number of Functional Gametes Produced
aspects.valueA: Four functional sperm cells from one primary spermatocyte.
aspects.valueB: Only one functional egg cell (plus polar bodies that degenerate) from one primary oocyte.

aspects.label: Timing
aspects.valueA: Begins at puberty and continues throughout adult male life.
aspects.valueB: Begins before birth (arrested), resumes at puberty, and ends at menopause.

aspects.label: Cytoplasm Division
aspects.valueA: Divides roughly equally among the four resulting sperm.
aspects.valueB: Divides unequally — the egg keeps almost all cytoplasm, polar bodies get very little.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Unequal cytoplasm division in oogenesis ensures the egg has enough nutrient reserves to support early embryonic development.
overlay.memoryTrick: Spermato- makes 4 equal sperm. Oo- makes 1 big egg plus tiny polar bodies.
overlay.commonMisconception: Oogenesis does not run continuously like spermatogenesis — it's largely arrested for years at a time (at prophase I) until hormonal signals trigger it to resume, one egg per cycle.
